network: The owner's laptop over the internet, outside us-west-2, assumption A25. Transfer times include that path.

endpoints.payer: Bucket owners. Every request was unsigned, so no requester was charged. A requester-pays bucket refuses unsigned requests.

tolerances.P1_pairing: Each primary product pairs with the Collection 1 item of the same datastrip. The product name with MSIL1C in place of MSIAQR names its Level-1C input. Earth Search's Level-1C item of that name declares a datastrip. The pair is the Collection 1 item of the same tile and platform whose datastrip has the same sensing start. A product without such an item is reported and left out. The older collection is not used.
tolerances.P2_grid: Every Collection 1 asset read must share the product's CRS and tile origin, from the file headers, within 1e-06 pixel at its own resolution. A scene that fails is left out of every comparison.
tolerances.P3_resampling: The primary product has one 20 m grid. A 20 m Collection 1 band is compared pixel for pixel. A 10 m band is the mean of the four 10 m pixels inside the 20 m pixel, used only when all four hold data. B01 at 60 m takes the 60 m pixel that contains the 20 m pixel.
tolerances.P4_units: Product values are divided by 10000. Collection 1 values are the stored integer times the scale plus the offset its asset declares. Differences are product minus Collection 1, in reflectance, and are reported in integer units of 1e-04.
tolerances.P5_comparable: A pixel is comparable in a band when the product value is not -32768 and the Collection 1 value, or each 10 m value it averages, is not 0.
tolerances.P6_strata: Results are reported per band and pixel class, interior, shoreline, and near-land, masks version 2 at 20 m. Two quality subsets: all comparable pixels, and both_clear_water, where the decoded ACOLITE flag integer is 0 and the scene classification is class 6. Each option's own flags define its own clear water.
tolerances.P7_disagreement: A pixel disagrees when the absolute difference exceeds 50 units, 0.005 reflectance. A band and class agrees when at least 90% of its comparable pixels do not disagree. Otherwise it differs. Pooled over scenes and lakes, per quality subset. This describes difference, not error. Neither product is a reference.
tolerances.P8_spread: Descriptive. Per scene-lake record with at least 100 comparable pixels, the median difference. Its spread across records is reported so that large lakes do not hide scene-to-scene variation.
tolerances.P9_offset_diagnostic: Diagnostic only, not a rule. Per scene, the declared Collection 1 offset, and the 1st and 50th percentiles of the stored B11 and B12 integers over interior pixels the scene classification calls water. It shows whether the declared offset matches the data. It never changes P4.

limitations: The 59 scenes are probe T4's: five tiles, one scene per tile and month of 2025, chosen from what the primary product holds. Its cloud screening removes most cloudy scenes.
Neither product is a reference. A difference is not an error in either. No in situ observation enters, and the comparison ranks neither correction, assumption A52.

The primary product averages its 10 m bands to 20 m. This probe averages the Collection 1 10 m bands over the same four pixels. B01 takes the containing 60 m pixel. Both are declared choices, rule P3, and add their own difference.
Pixel classes come from NHD polygons, whose shorelines are not observations of a given date.
Pooled statistics are pixel observations summed over scenes. Large lakes dominate them. The summary also splits by tile and size and reports the spread of per-record medians.
Quantiles come from integer histograms of 1e-04 bins, clipped at plus or minus 0.5. The clipped count is reported per stratum.
GDAL requests and bytes are byte ranges requested, from its debug log. Laptop over the internet, outside us-west-2, assumption A25. Times are not production estimates.
No pixel value is stored. Only counts and statistics.
